NST: non-specific ST-segment changes. non-specific ST-segment elevation or depression.
ISCAL: ischemic ST-T changes in anterolateral leads
ISCIN: ischemic ST-T changes in inferior leads
HYP: cardiac hypertrophy or chamber enlargement. left ventricular hypertrophy, right ventricular hypertrophy, biventricular hypertrophy, or atrial enlargement.
CD: cardiac conduction disturbance. atrioventricular block, including first-degree, second-degree, and third-degree atrioventricular block; right or left bundle branch block, fascicular block, and intraventricular conduction delay.
ISCIL: ischemic ST-T changes in inferolateral leads
ISCI: inferior or inferolateral ischemic ST-T changes
ISCAS: ischemic ST-T changes in anteroseptal leads
ISCA: anterior, anteroseptal, anterolateral, or lateral ischemic ST-T changes
ISCLA: ischemic ST-T changes in lateral leads
ANEUR: ST-T changes compatible with ventricular aneurysm
EL: electrolyte disturbance or drug-related ST-T effect
ISCAN: ischemic ST-T changes in anterior leads
2AVB: second-degree atrioventricular block. mobitz type I or Mobitz type II second-degree atrioventricular block.
VCLVH: QRS voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy
LVOLT: low QRS voltages in frontal and horizontal leads
BIGU: bigeminal pattern of unspecified supraventricular or ventricular origin
TRIGU: trigeminal pattern of unspecified supraventricular or ventricular origin
2AVB1: second-degree atrioventricular block, Mobitz type I
2AVB2: second-degree atrioventricular block, Mobitz type II
AVB: Atrioventricular block. First-degree, second-degree, or third-degree atrioventricular block.
LBBBB: left posterior bundle-branch or fascicular block
LFBBB: left anterior bundle-branch or fascicular block
LVQRSAL: low QRS voltage in all leads
LVQRSCL: low QRS voltage in chest leads
LVQRSLL: low QRS voltage in limb leads
STTC: ST-T changes. ST-segment and T-wave abnormalities, including ST-segment elevation, upward ST-segment displacement, ST-segment depression, T-wave inversion, and other T-wave changes.
TWC: T-wave changes. Abnormal T-wave morphology, including flattened, inverted, or biphasic T waves.
